en: 3. The Question on the Kalandaka’s Limb “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘one limb of the kalandaka should be adopted,’ which is that one limb that should be adopted?
“Just as, O King, when an enemy pounces upon him, the kalandaka lashes its tail, makes it large, and with that very tail-bulwark repels the enemy;”

In the same way, Great King, when the enemy of the defilements falls upon him, a practitioner of yoga should brandish the mallet of mindfulness, making it large, and with that very mallet of mindfulness, all defilements must be warded off.
This, Great King, is one quality of the squirrel that should be adopted.
And this was said, Great King, by the Elder Cūḷapanthaka:
with the mallet of the foundations of mindfulness— ”
“They must be slain again and again.
Thus ends the third question on the Kalandakaṅga.
